name: SOMA
funding: Civil non-profit association (Asociación Civil) funded by artist philanthropy, Fundación Jumex grants, Prince Claus Fund, and tuition-free educational patronage.
watch: Counter-institutional space founded in 2009 by a collective of artists led by Yoshua Okón.

name: Staatliche Museen zu Berlin
funding: Federal government pays 71% of the Prussian Cultural Heritage Foundation's €275M operating budget, Berlin 14%, other Länder 7%. Sparkassen-Finanzgruppe is main sponsor, renewed in 2017.
watch: Governed under the Prussian Cultural Heritage Foundation (SPK). Major public funding; corporate partnerships are regulated by federal public procurement and anti-corruption guidelines, though historic colonial provenance remains under active restitution review.
records_note: Parent SPK posts annual reports 2016 to 2025 and budget figures; SMB names only supporter groups and patrons undated, and no council members.

name: Storefront for Art and Architecture
funding: 501(c)(3) non-profit organization supported by Graham Foundation, Andy Warhol Foundation, NYSCA, and individual members.

name: Stroom Den Haag
funding: Municipality of The Hague cultural allocation, Mondriaan Fund, public research grants.

name: Sun Mu Studio & North Korean Dissident Art Archive
watch: Studio and archive of the pseudonymous North Korean defector artist Sun Mu ('No Line / Border'). His work satirises Kim dynasty totalitarianism and records defector experiences.

name: Swiss Institute
funding: Pro Helvetia, NYSCA and NYC Cultural Affairs (2025-26); Warhol, Arison Arts, Frankenthaler, LUMA and Goldsmith foundations. Blavatnik Family Foundation gave in 2020 and 2021, Bloomberg Philanthropies in 2018 and 2019.
watch: Bloomberg (2018-19) and Blavatnik Family Foundation (2020-21) were partners; neither is listed since, so neither is a current funder.
records_note: No annual reports found; 990s are on ProPublica, partners are named by year from 2018 to 2026, and the board is listed.

name: Tainan Art Museum
funding: Administrative corporation. 2025 revenue NT$201M: Tainan City subsidy NT$89.7M, Ministry of Culture and others NT$25M, tickets and parking NT$57M, donations NT$3.7M.
watch: Opened 27 January 2019. In 2025 the Ministry of Culture set up a preparatory office for a planned Tainan National Art Museum.
records_note: Publishes annual reports 2019 to 2024, final accounts 2017 to 2025 and yearly donor lists to 2025; names only its chair, not the full board.

name: Taipei Fine Arts Museum
funding: Taipei City agency; 2025-26 sponsors incl. CTBC Culture & Education Fdn (bank), Chanel, Friends of TFAM, Winsing Arts Fdn, Luce Fdn.
watch: Dec 2021: Venice pavilion paused over Sakuliu assault claims; victim's lawyer said TFAM's name was used to pressure her.
records_note: Annual reports 2006 to 2024, yearly budget and final accounts 2014 to 2025 and a dated sponsor directory are on its site; no board.

name: TANK Shanghai
funding: Founded by collector and karaoke-club owner Qiao Zhibing, who told The Art Newspaper he paid for it. The government-backed West Bund Group invited him and manages the surrounding park.
watch: Opened in March 2019 in five former aviation fuel tanks. Time Out says Qiao invested with West Bund Group; no budget was found.
records_note: Its site names a four-person council led by founder Qiao Zhibing; it posts no annual reports, accounts or funder list.

name: TarraWarra Museum of Art
funding: Founded by Marc and Eva Besen (retail), whose family foundation endows it. Sponsors: Arnold Bloch Leibler, Chubb, Aon, Four Pillars Gin. Victoria and Yarra Ranges Council fund education.
watch: First major privately endowed public museum in Australia (Yarra Valley).
records_note: Names its eight-member board and shows sponsors as undated logos; its policies page posts no annual reports or accounts.

name: Temple Bar Gallery + Studios
funding: Arts Council is principal funder. Grants from Dublin City Council, Culture Ireland and others; corporate partners Henry J Lyons, Arthur Cox and Dublin Port; RTÉ Supporting the Arts.
watch: Artist-founded and artist-led non-profit trust in central Dublin.
records_note: No annual report; posts 2025 audited accounts and a 13-member board, and names its Arts Council principal funder, grant funders and three corporate partners, undated.

name: Tensta konsthall
funding: Swedish Arts Council (Kulturrådet), City of Stockholm, Region Stockholm. Complete non-profit accounting.
watch: In the modernist Stockholm suburb of Tensta; its programme deals with migration, working-class housing struggles and civic solidarity.
